source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 91(3), published p.295, Abstract: an external stop signal or an error can start a stopping process that races the processes underlying ongoing thought/action; the winner determines inhibition versus completion

Psychological Review 91(3), published pp.296-299, illustrative stop-signal choice-RT experiment: stop signal occurs on a subset of trials at variable delays after primary-stimulus onset; measured outcomes include inhibition probability, no-signal RT, signal-respond RT, and internal stop-signal RT

Psychological Review 91(3), published p.299, formal race-model introduction: primary-task and stopping finishing times are treated as independent random variables; inhibition is stochastic and reflects the probability that stopping finishes first

Psychological Review 91(3), published pp.300-302, inhibition-function and signal-respond-RT derivations: stop-signal delay shifts relative finishing time, predicts response probability and signal-respond RT, and permits inference about the covert stopping latency from observed timing distributions

conditions: a primary-task process is initiated by the primary stimulus and, on some trials, a later explicit stop signal initiates a stopping process
the formal race account treats primary-task and stopping-process finishing times as independent random variables
population: human participants in explicit stop-signal reaction-time data sets, including three experienced adult subjects in the source's illustrative experiment
task: perform the speeded primary response unless a later stop signal requires cancellation
temporal_scope: the primary-task process begins at primary-stimulus onset; the stop signal can occur after a variable delay and initiates the stopping process
trial outcome depends on the relative finishing times of the two processes; the covert duration from stop-signal onset to completion of stopping is inferred rather than directly observed

nodes.description: process that carries the primary task toward the overt response
experimentally presented signal that initiates the stopping process in the explicit stop-signal paradigm
internal process initiated by the stop signal whose finishing time races the primary-task finishing time
formal-model assumption that the primary-task and stopping finishing times are independent random variables
latent ordering of the primary-task and stopping-process finishing times on a stop-signal trial
whether the primary response is inhibited or escapes inhibition and is executed
observed stop-signal delay, probability of responding or inhibiting, no-signal reaction-time distribution, and signal-respond reaction times used by the formal account
covert time from stop-signal onset to completion of the stopping process, estimated from the race model rather than directly observed
procedure varying the delay between primary-stimulus onset and stop-signal onset while observing response probability and reaction-time distributions

relations.description: presentation of the explicit stop signal initiates the stopping process in the source's experimental paradigm
the formal derivation treats the two finishing times as independent random variables rather than as an interacting sequential mechanism
the response is inhibited when stopping finishes first and is executed when the primary-task process finishes first
in the explicit stop-signal task, primary-task processing begins at the primary stimulus and a later stop signal starts the stopping process after the experimentally varied delay
varying stop-signal delay yields the inhibition function and associated reaction-time measurements predicted by the race account
the formal race relations permit the covert stopping latency to be estimated from observed response probabilities, reaction-time distributions, and stop-signal delay
